subject: Renewal proposal — 3yr accelerator with phased rollback
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal — 3yr accelerator with phased rollback

Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the time last week — attached is a concise draft of the renewal we discussed. High level proposal:

- Term: 36 months (3yr) with staged ramp across yr1->yr3 to match usage growth.
- Capacity uplift: +45% baseline tokens across all inference routes, with two scheduled mid-term capacity increases (M+9 and M+21).
- Auto-renew: optional auto-renew on year 3 with a 60-day opt-out window pre-expiry.
- Phased rollback: limited rollback clause (see section 4) that allows scale-back within the first 180 days of yr2 if usage materially undershoots agreed forecasts (with prorated credits).
- Billing: quarterly invoicing with an option to annualize for 2% discount.

Action items in the PDF: mutual action plan, signature blocks, and a short procurement checklist.

Attachments: ACME_Renewal_Draft_20250714.pdf (draft contract + MA plan)

If that looks good I recommend a technical/finance call this Thursday to lock cadence and invoicing. Availability: 10–12 or 14–16 PT.

Best,

Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — 3yr accelerator with phased rollback

Thanks Marissa —

Appreciate the clear draft. A few immediate questions from our side:

1) Proration: if we hit the M+9 capacity increase, how is billing prorated for that quarter? We prefer per-day proration rather than whole-quarter adjustments.
2) Rollback: the 180-day rollback looks reasonable but procurement wants clearer guardrails on what qualifies as "material undershoot" — can you add an objective metric (e.g., <60% of forecasted monthly token consumption for two consecutive months)?
3) Invoice cadence: procurement asks if we can keep monthly invoices until the end of year 1, then switch to quarterly thereafter.

I'll loop legal if we get alignment on proration and the rollback metric. Procurement copied here (procure@acme-ai.com) — they might propose slight changes to payment terms.

I'll attach a short SOW outline we use internally for renewals.

Thanks —
Elaine Park

Elaine / Marissa —

Thanks for the notes. From a legal/ops perspective I propose the following concrete edits we can include in the next draft:

- Proration: per-day proration for mid-period capacity changes (we'll calculate on active days in the billing cycle).
- Rollback metric: define "material undershoot" as <60% of agreed forecast for two consecutive billing months. If triggered, allow one rollback instance within the first 180 days of year 2 with automatic prorated credit to the following invoice (credit applies only against future usage charges, not previously paid invoices).
- Invoice cadence: accept monthly invoicing for year 1 transitioning to quarterly; include auto-switch clause and notice period (30 days).
- Service credit: if rollout or capacity increases fail to meet SLOs (latency/availability thresholds in Appendix B) for >5% of calls over a 30-day window post-activation, customer receives a service credit up to 10% of that quarter's usage fees.

I've attached a redlined doc for faster review: redlines_redwood_v1.docx

If procurement is comfortable with these guardrails we can produce a final tracked-changes copy tomorrow and loop legal for signature.

Thanks,
